name: Eglon
overview: Eglon was a male king of Moab who played a significant role in Israel's history during a period when the Israelites were oppressed. Because Israel again did evil in the sight of the LORD, they were sold into Eglon's hands for eighteen years, marking a time of subjugation under his rule.
namesAndTitles: The name Eglon means "circle" or "young bull," reflecting a proper name without divine attribution. Additionally, he held the title "King of Moab," indicating his royal authority over the Moabite people during this period.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Eglon beyond what is noted in his role as king and oppressor of Israel. There are no further relational details provided in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Eglon's significance lies in his role as an instrument of God's judgment upon Israel when they turned away from Him. His oppression of Israel for eighteen years underscores the consequences of Israel's persistent disobedience. As King of Moab, Eglon’s dominance highlights the challenges Israel faced before God raised deliverers to rescue His people.
